source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: The Pole Star appears nearly stationary because Earth's rotation axis points very close to it, while other stars appear to move around it.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Stars make circular trails around the Pole Star during the night because Earth revolves around the Sun.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Other stars actually orbit the Pole Star.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Earth rotates because the stars moving around the Pole Star make it turn.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The Pole Star is visible as the nearly stationary centre of star trails in both hemispheres.

intelligence.enrichment: Because Earth's rotation axis points very close to the Pole Star in the Northern Hemisphere, the Pole Star appears nearly stationary and other stars appear to move around it. Earth's rotation plus the direction of its axis makes most stars trace apparent circular paths around the nearly fixed Pole Star. The learner correctly applies this rule: Because Earth's rotation axis points very close to the Pole Star in the Northern Hemisphere, the Pole Star appears nearly stationary and other stars appear to move around it. All stars should move across the sky in the same way because they are all in the night sky.
